EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
The most critical development in the past 24 hours is the provisional agreement between Iran and Oman for a temporary joint maritime corridor and mine-clearing operation in the Strait of Hormuz, signaling a formalization of navigation protocols amid ongoing tensions. Concurrently, former President Trump declared the Strait cleared of Iranian mines, threatening immediate destruction for any new attempts at obstruction, indicating a continued robust US posture.

IRAN
Iran's Deputy Foreign Minister, Kazem Garibabadi, and Foreign Minister Abbas Aragchi announced a temporary agreement with Oman for a joint maritime corridor and mine-clearing in the Strait of Hormuz. Garibabadi stated the southern route of the Strait would be closed and this has been agreed upon by Oman, to be announced to the International Maritime Organization. He emphasized that the Strait's reopening is conditional on the US fulfilling its obligations, ending the war on all fronts, lifting the blockade, and resolving the situation in Yemen, and that the two countries must negotiate a new permanent route within 30 to 60 days. Under the agreement, military vessels will not be permitted to transit the Strait of Hormuz, with passage limited to commercial ships. Press TV reports indicate Iran maintains full control over the entry route and part of the exit route. The Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesman, Esmail Baghaei, warned that US sanctions are an attack on the sovereignty of all nations. Internally, Iran faces severe economic strain, with widespread reports of fuel shortages, kilometer-long queues at gas stations in Tehran, and significant price increases for basic goods and services. Several sources (@mamlekate, @kianmeli1) report public discontent, with some claiming gasoline quality is poor and economic pressure is effective. President Pezeshkian acknowledged economic shortcomings, stating the war must end, and Parliament Speaker Qalibaf warned against solely relying on military power without addressing the public's economic needs. The US Secret Service is investigating an Iranian state TV video discussing a potential plot to assassinate Trump's son, Baron Trump, including a reported $10 million reward.

ISRAEL
IDF Chief of Staff Lt. Gen. Eyal Zamir visited the Gaza Strip, stating the pursuit of October 7 terrorists continues and Israel will not allow enemies in Gaza and Lebanon to rebuild strength, vowing to eliminate threats offensively and systematically. The IDF and Shin Bet jointly reported striking five Hamas weapon depots located in mosques and near aid sites, along with a rocket launch site, in Gaza yesterday, citing Hamas's cynical use of civilian infrastructure. In the West Bank, Religious Zionism MK Zvi Sukkot, accompanied by IDF protection, was filmed smashing a Palestinian "Martyrs' Monument" in Madama village. The IDF condemned Sukkot's actions as "deceptive and manipulative" and a "complete overstepping of authority," stating the tour was approved but the demolition was not. Prime Minister Netanyahu condemned the act, emphasizing that the IDF is sovereign in Judea and Samaria and public officials should not take the law into their own hands. Defense Minister Israel Katz affirmed Israel will not withdraw from the Golan Heights or the security zone as long as jihadist threats persist. Politically, Likud is undergoing a recount of votes in Beer Yaakov due to fraud allegations, potentially impacting the final list. Ofer Winter announced a new party, "Amcha Israel," with Joseph Haddad, aiming for the role of Defense Minister. Benny Gantz is reportedly facing another defection from his new political framework.

GAZA & WEST BANK
IDF Chief of Staff Lt. Gen. Eyal Zamir reiterated the commitment to pursue October 7 terrorists in Gaza. The IDF and Shin Bet confirmed strikes on five Hamas weapon depots and a rocket launch site in Gaza yesterday, emphasizing that these facilities were located within mosques and near humanitarian infrastructure, constituting "a clear warning" against terror activity. In the West Bank, MK Zvi Sukkot destroyed a Palestinian "Martyrs' Monument" in Madama village while under IDF escort. The IDF strongly criticized Sukkot's actions, stating it was a deviation from the approved tour and that they had planned to demolish the monument in a systematic manner soon. A cabinet discussion on West Bank escalation was held, with the Central Command chief expressing concern over violence by Jewish extremists. Ten weapons were seized, and two suspects from Jericho were arrested, thwarting a smuggling attempt across the Jordan border.

LEBANON
The IDF launched airstrikes in southern Lebanon, with reports indicating targets in Nabatieh, Kfarmatta, Rumaan, Ali Taher, Al-Mansouri, Zarbin, and Al-Qantara. Press TV reported Israeli forces targeted displaced Lebanese homes in Al-Mansouri.

SYRIA & IRAQ
N12 reported IDF forces, including over 10 vehicles, operating in the Gamla village area in southwestern Syria. Turkish President Erdogan commented on tensions with Israel in Syria, stating Turkey will not compromise on its principles or national interests and aims for peace and justice in the region, rejecting hidden agendas. Mazloum Abdi, Commander of the Kurdish forces (SDF) in Syria, announced the dissolution of the organization and autonomous administration, stating the forces have fully integrated into the Syrian state; later sources from @sharghdaily indicate Abdi was appointed as a special advisor to the head of the Syrian government (Jolani) for Kurdish affairs. The JGC Japanese company is preparing to resume its FCC project in Basra, Iraq, by early September.

GULF STATES
Oman's Foreign Minister Badr Al-Busaidi visited Tehran to discuss arrangements for navigation in the Strait of Hormuz, with Iran announcing a temporary joint maritime corridor and mine-clearing plan. Saudi Arabia's cabinet, chaired by King Salman, emphasized the importance of keeping the Strait of Hormuz and Bab al-Mandeb open and safe, supporting diplomatic solutions and freedom of navigation. The Trump administration submitted a civil nuclear cooperation agreement with Saudi Arabia to Congress, contingent on Saudi Arabia joining the Abraham Accords and recognizing Israel. Qatar's Foreign Ministry spokesperson stated Qatar supports ongoing mediation efforts and opposes unilateral sanctions on Iran. Pakistan is actively mediating US-Iran talks, with its Army Chief Asim Munir meeting Iranian officials, reportedly conveying a US offer to lift the blockade and sanctions in exchange for reopening Hormuz and ending proxy attacks.

KEY DEVELOPMENTS
1.  **Strait of Hormuz Agreement**: Iran and Oman announced a temporary agreement for a joint maritime corridor and mine-clearing in the Strait, with Iran's Deputy FM stating the southern route will be closed and negotiations for a permanent system within 30-60 days.
2.  **Trump's Hormuz Claims and Threats**: Former President Trump claimed the US Navy cleared all mines from international waters in the Strait of Hormuz and threatened immediate destruction of any vessel planting new mines.
3.  **MK Sukkot's West Bank Monument Destruction**: Israeli MK Zvi Sukkot, under IDF escort, smashed a Palestinian monument in Madama, drawing strong condemnation from the IDF and PM Netanyahu for acting deceptively and without authority.
4.  **IDF Gaza Operations**: The IDF and Shin Bet reported striking five Hamas weapon depots located in mosques and near humanitarian sites, and a rocket launch site in the Gaza Strip.
5.  **Iran's Economic Crisis & Protests**: Widespread reports of fuel shortages, kilometer-long queues at gas stations, skyrocketing prices, and general public discontent across Iran due to economic pressures and war.
6.  **CIA Director John Ratcliffe's Moscow Visit**: CIA Director John Ratcliffe made an unannounced four-hour visit to Moscow, reportedly delivering an ultimatum regarding drone incursions into NATO territory.
7.  **US Diplomatic Return to Middle East**: The New York Times reported the US is preparing to return diplomats to its Middle East embassies, indicating a potential de-escalation of direct military conflict.
8.  **SDF Dissolution in Syria**: Mazloum Abdi announced the formal dissolution of the Syrian Democratic Forces (SDF) and its autonomous administration, integrating its elements into the Syrian state, with Abdi taking an advisory role.
9.  **Pakistan's Mediation Efforts**: Pakistan's Army Chief Asim Munir met with Iranian officials, reportedly conveying a US offer to halt the naval blockade and lift sanctions in return for Iran reopening the Strait of Hormuz and ceasing proxy attacks.

THREAT ASSESSMENT
Escalation risks remain high in the Strait of Hormuz, despite the temporary Iran-Oman agreement, as former President Trump's strong statements and threats against new mine-laying could lead to immediate military responses. The economic distress and public unrest in Iran, exacerbated by US sanctions, pose a significant internal stability risk that could spill over into regional actions. The West Bank is an active flashpoint, with settler violence (as highlighted by the Sukkot incident and Israeli cabinet discussions) risking further widespread escalation, especially given the IDF's stated commitment to dismantling "terror infrastructure." The potential for miscalculation regarding Iranian proxy actions in the region, particularly after US intelligence indicated "unprecedented damage" from Iranian missile and drone attacks on US sites, remains a red line for US military engagement.

REGIONAL & INTERNATIONAL RESPONSE
**United States**: Secretary of State Marco Rubio indicated the US is unlikely to initiate new attacks against Iran "for now," focusing instead on economic pressure. The Trump administration imposed new sanctions, with Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent describing them as an "economic D-Day" aimed at severing Iran's economic lifelines, although he downplayed immediate "blowing up the global financial system." The US is reportedly preparing to return diplomats to Middle Eastern embassies evacuated during the Iran war. Former President Trump claimed US Navy cleared all Hormuz mines and threatened destruction for new ones, calling Iran's killing of protestors a "humanitarian crisis."
**Gulf States**: Oman is actively engaging Iran on Hormuz navigation. Saudi Arabia is pursuing a civil nuclear deal with the US, linked to recognizing Israel. Qatar and China warned against unilateral sanctions on Iran, stating they could intensify regional tensions.
**United Kingdom**: Treasury Secretary John Healey supported US efforts, calling for continued economic pressure on Iran and action to reopen Hormuz.
**China**: Opposed new US sanctions, stating cooperation with Iran is within international law and will not be disrupted, vowing to protect its interests.
**Pakistan**: Army Chief Asim Munir engaged in mediation between the US and Iran, presenting a proposal to Iranian officials for US sanctions relief in exchange for Hormuz reopening and an end to proxy attacks.
**Turkey**: President Erdogan criticized Israel regarding Syria, reaffirming Turkish national interests and denying hidden agendas. The Bloomberg report suggests Turkey, seeking F-35s/F-16s, is unlikely to anger Trump by maintaining extensive trade with Iran.

INTELLIGENCE NOTES
There are contradictions in reporting regarding the status of US-Iran negotiations and the Hormuz situation. Iranian officials describe a new "temporary agreement" with Oman for navigation and mine-clearing, implying a formalized diplomatic process. However, former President Trump's immediate claim that all mines have already been cleared by the US Navy and his unilateral threats of destruction for future mine-laying suggest a US posture that may not fully align with an ongoing bilateral (Iran-Oman) diplomatic solution. There is also a contradiction concerning MK Sukkot's actions: the IDF states the monument destruction was "deceptive and manipulative" and "without authority," yet another IDF source noted the tour was approved, and a separate source mentions the IDF had planned to demolish the monument soon anyway. Unverified claims include the alleged Iranian video threatening Trump's son, with US Secret Service confirming awareness but not authenticity or source definitively. Propaganda indicators are present in both US and Iranian statements, with the US Treasury Secretary's "economic D-Day" rhetoric being mocked by Iranian Parliament Speaker Qalibaf, and Iranian media framing US diplomatic maneuvers as "retreats." There are reporting gaps on the specifics of the new US sanctions (apart from impacting 60 entities) and the exact mechanism or timeline for the Iran-Oman Hormuz agreement. The extensive reporting on Iran's internal economic hardship and public discontent from multiple Iranian channels (e.g., @kianmeli1, @mamlekate, @VahidOnline) appears consistent and likely reflects genuine challenges.
